title: Breaking bad news by telephone

header.contentArea: Communication skills in giving and receiving information; confidentiality and remote consultation

brief.setting: Telephone call from a side room
brief.scenario: Mr Felix Norwood, 64, is awaiting urgent histology results after a biopsy. Face-to-face review is not possible today.
brief.task: Explain the result to him safely by telephone. The examiner may ask you questions at the end.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Confirm who you're speaking to and that it's safe to talk, then give the news in small, clear steps.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Rushing to the diagnosis, or disclosing results before confirming identity and privacy.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: Confirm his identity, then ask if it's a safe, private time to talk.

flow: Deliver information in stages, with pauses

grid.label: Confirming identity and privacy
grid.fail: Discloses or discusses the result before confirming who he is speaking to.
grid.pass: Confirms his identity and asks whether it's a safe, private time to talk.
grid.high: Also asks whether anyone else is present whom he'd like involved before continuing.

grid.label: Checking existing understanding
grid.fail: Assumes what he already knows and launches straight into the result.
grid.pass: Asks what he already understands about why he's having this call.
grid.high: Uses his answer to judge how much of a warning shot he needs and paces accordingly.

grid.label: Warning shot and clear language
grid.fail: Gives the result abruptly, or opens with technical pathology language.
grid.pass: Gives a warning shot, then uses clear, direct language and avoids jargon and euphemisms.
grid.high: Chooses words that are honest but not brutal, and checks he's ready before saying the actual result.

grid.label: Pacing and allowing reaction
grid.fail: Delivers all the information in one block without pausing.
grid.pass: Gives information in small sections, pausing between them and allowing silence.
grid.high: Actively listens for and responds to his emotional reaction before moving on.

grid.label: Staying within known facts
grid.fail: Gives a prognosis or survival estimate not supported by the information available.
grid.pass: Gives only the information that is confirmed and avoids speculating on prognosis.
grid.high: Explains plainly what is and isn't known yet, without minimising or overstating either way.

grid.label: Checking understanding and closing
grid.fail: Ends the call without checking what he has understood.
grid.pass: Asks what he has understood and answers his questions before ending the call.
grid.high: Asks if he'd like a relative or friend involved going forward and checks how he wants to be contacted next.

grid.label: Next steps and safety-net
grid.fail: Ends the call without a follow-up plan or contact route.
grid.pass: Explains immediate next steps, who will contact him, and gives a reliable contact route.
grid.high: Arranges face-to-face follow-up where appropriate and recognises when the call should be escalated to a face-to-face review instead.

grid.label: Documentation
grid.fail: Doesn't record that the conversation took place.
grid.pass: Documents the conversation, including what was said and his response.
grid.high: Also records the agreed follow-up plan and who else was informed.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The call connects. Patient: "Is this about my biopsy?"

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, I'm afraid the biopsy shows cancer.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: There's a mass with malignant histological features and likely lymphovascular invasion, so the staging will need further imaging.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Honestly, with this type it's usually only a matter of months.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Someone will probably be in touch at some point. That's everything from me.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I don't think that's necessary, it was just a phone call.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Hello, could I confirm I'm speaking with Mr Norwood, and is this a safe, private time for a call about your results?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Patient: "Yes, that's fine. Is this about my biopsy?"

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It is. Can I ask what you've been told so far about why we're doing this test?

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Patient: "Just that they were checking for something serious."

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'm afraid I do have some difficult news about the result. The biopsy shows changes that are concerning for cancer.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Patient is silent for a moment.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll pause there — take your time. I know that's a lot to hear.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I understand why you're asking, but I don't have enough information yet to answer that — we need further tests before we know more.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Can you tell me what you've understood from what I've said, and do you have any questions right now?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The team will contact you within the next couple of days to arrange further tests and a face-to-face appointment, and here's a direct number if you need us before then.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'll write up exactly what we've discussed today in your notes.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Hello, could I first confirm I'm speaking with Mr Norwood himself, and check this is a safe, private time to talk? Is anyone with you that you'd like involved?

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Patient: "It's just me, that's fine. Is this about my biopsy?"

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It is. Before I go on, what have you been told so far, and how have you been feeling waiting for this call?

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Patient: "Just that they were checking for something serious. I've been dreading this."

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'm sorry, I do have some difficult news. The biopsy result shows changes that are concerning for cancer.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll give you a moment — I can hear that's hit you hard.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That's completely understandable to want to know, but honestly I don't have enough information yet — we need further scans and tests before anyone can give you a realistic answer, and I don't want to guess.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Can you tell me in your own words what you've taken from this, and is there anything I can go over again?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Given how much this is to take in over the phone, I'd like to arrange a face-to-face appointment soon so we can go through everything properly, with someone with you if you'd like; the team will call within two days, and here's a direct number in the meantime.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'll document today's call in full, including how you responded and the follow-up plan, so the whole team is aware.

failures.move: Discussing the result before confirming identity or privacy.
failures.consequence: Confidential information may be disclosed to the wrong person, or in a setting that isn't safe for him to receive it.

failures.move: Opening with technical pathology language or no warning shot.
failures.consequence: The patient is shocked by jargon before he has any chance to prepare for bad news.

failures.move: Giving a survival estimate not supported by the available information.
failures.consequence: An unfounded prognosis can cause lasting harm and may be wrong once full staging is known.

failures.move: Ending the call without a follow-up plan or contact route.
failures.consequence: Leaves him alone with serious news and no way to seek support or ask further questions.

recovery.when: You've launched into the result too fast
recovery.line: I should have checked first — is this a safe, private time, and can I ask what you already understood before I go further?

recovery.when: Asked for a prognosis you can't support
recovery.line: I don't want to guess at something this important — we need more information before anyone can answer that properly.

knowledge.fact: Confirm identity and that it is a safe, private time before disclosing confidential information by phone.
Give a warning shot, use clear language, and pause between sections to allow silence and reaction.
Remote consultation is acceptable only when the mode is suitable for the purpose; escalate to face-to-face review when it is not.
Document the conversation, including the information given and the patient's response.

recall.think: Confidential, serious news given to the wrong person, or without support in place, causes real harm.
recall.say: "I'm afraid I have some difficult news about your results."
do: Warning shot, then clear language, paused
Arrange follow-up and a contact route

numbers.meaning: Year GMC Good medical practice (communication standards) took effect

recall.trap: Assuming feeling awkward about a difficult call justifies rushing through it.
recall.finish: Face-to-face follow-up arranged where appropriate; conversation documented.

sources.name: GMC: Good medical practice
sources.supports: Doctors must communicate clearly, respectfully and in a way that supports patients to understand and make decisions, and must keep clear, accurate records

sources.name: GMC: Confidentiality — good practice in handling patient information
sources.version: Effective 25 April 2017; updated 25 May 2018 and 13 December 2024
sources.supports: Verify the identity of the person you are speaking to and satisfy yourself it is appropriate to disclose confidential information before doing so, including by telephone

sources.name: GMC: How our professional standards can be applied to remote consultations
sources.supports: Remote consultation is appropriate only when it is a suitable way of meeting the patient's needs; escalate to a face-to-face consultation when it is not

partner.opening: The candidate is making a telephone call to Mr Norwood about an urgent histology result. Please begin when you're ready.
partner.actorBrief: You are Felix Norwood, 64, waiting anxiously for a biopsy result. You are alone at home. Opening line, once identity and privacy are confirmed: "Is this about my biopsy?" You are calm at first but become quiet and subdued once told it's cancer-related, and you ask directly how long you have left. If the candidate gives jargon or rushes, ask them to slow down or explain in plain terms. If handled with a warning shot, clear language and pauses, you become able to ask sensible questions about what happens next. Hidden concern, revealed only if asked how you're feeling or what worries you: you live alone and are frightened about managing at home if you need more treatment.

reveals.trigger: Asks what he already knows or how he's been feeling
reveals.finding: "Just that they were checking for something serious. I've been dreading this call."

reveals.trigger: Asks if he'd like anyone else involved
reveals.finding: "It's just me here — I live alone."
"I'm frightened about managing on my own if I need more treatment."

push.question: How long has he got?
push.expect: Doesn't speculate; explains further tests are needed before anyone can answer that.

push.question: How will you follow this call up?
push.expect: Arranges a face-to-face appointment, a contact route, and further tests, with a timeframe.

push.question: What will you record afterwards?
push.expect: Documents the conversation, his response, and the agreed follow-up plan.

curveballs.prompt: A woman answers his phone and says: "I'm his daughter, you can tell me."
curveballs.safeAnswer: Doesn't disclose confidential information until speaking to Mr Norwood himself or confirming his consent for her to be told.
Acknowledges the question honestly, explains this isn't yet known, and avoids giving an unsupported figure.

curveballs.prompt: He starts crying and goes silent on the call.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Pauses, allows the silence, and checks gently whether he wants to continue now or have someone call him back shortly.

curveballs.prompt: "Should this have been done face to face?"
curveballs.safeAnswer: Acknowledges telephone has limits, explains why it was necessary today, and offers a face-to-face follow-up soon.
